title: Your headphones make sound to ERASE sound
keywords_note: *word* = red (noise), ~word~ = cyan (anti-noise / fix), ^word^ = amber (key idea). Per-scene speed/pitch = tone of voice.

scenes.text: Your headphones are secretly making *sound* to ^erase^ sound!
Picture a plane. That *engine* *roar* is slamming into your ears, nonstop.

scenes.label: SQUEEZE · STRETCH
scenes.text: Every sound is a ^wave^ of air, squeezing and stretching hundreds of times every second.

scenes.label: OUTSIDE MIC
scenes.text: So, tiny ^microphones^ on the outside of each earcup record the *noise* before it reaches you.

scenes.label: ANTI-NOISE
scenes.text: A chip copies that wave, ^flips^ it upside down, and the speaker plays this ~anti-noise~ in a split second!
Where the noise *pushes*, the anti-noise ~pulls~. Peak meets valley, and they ^cancel^ out!

scenes.label: INSIDE MIC
scenes.text: A second mic inside the cup listens to whatever is left, and ~fixes~ the mistakes.

scenes.label: TOO FAST!
scenes.text: But it's not perfect. Sudden sounds, like a *dog* *bark*, change too fast to predict.
That's why engines ^vanish^, but voices still sneak through. Follow for more!
